Expected: Left-clicking the tray icon opens one XClip popup, restores it from minimized state, and brings it to front.
Ctrl+Shift+V opens the existing instance and does not create a duplicate tray icon or process.
Opening through the global hotkey captures the previously active external window as the paste target.
Enter writes the selected clip, hides XClip, restores the target, and sends Ctrl+V exactly once.
Double-clicking a clip follows the same direct-paste path as Enter.
Ctrl+C and the Copy-only action update the clipboard without sending Ctrl+V.
Typing in Search refreshes results after debounce without freezing the UI or showing stale results.
Visible matching text is highlighted without changing stored clipboard content.
All, Pinned, and Recent return only the expected entries and preserve deterministic ordering.
TEXT, CODE, URL, PATH, JSON, and COMMAND filters return only matching clips.
Reset restores All scope, no type filter, and the current search contract without selection corruption.
No-history and no-results states are readable, centered, and keyboard-safe.
Every visible clip has the correct restrained badge and recycled cells never mix badges or content.
A valid HTTP(S) clip opens in the default browser; invalid or non-HTTP schemes are rejected.
An existing path is revealed in Explorer and executable or script paths are never launched.
Valid object or array JSON is copied pretty-printed; invalid or scalar JSON is rejected.
COMMAND clips are copied only and are never executed by XClip.
Pin/unpin updates persistence, section placement, accent state, and selection without data loss.
F2 can set or clear a pinned title without modifying the original clipboard content.
Alt+Up/Down and menu ordering persist across reload and application restart.
Ctrl toggle and Shift range selection remain stable across scrolling and section headings.
Batch actions preserve visible order and use the documented separator without losing individual clips.
Clear removes only visible non-pinned clips described by the confirmation and protects pinned or hidden clips.
Single delete is immediate; multi-delete requires confirmation; Cancel is the destructive default.
Pause state stays synchronized between popup and tray, and resume does not ingest the clipboard snapshot.
Settings opens modally, applies valid values, rejects invalid values, and preserves focus and watcher state.
Quick Help lists the frozen shortcuts, is keyboard reachable, and remains inside the current monitor.
Row, Actions, split-button, and tray menus close on selection, Escape, or outside interaction without becoming stuck.
A 500000-character clip stays bounded to the frozen preview limits and does not expand the whole viewport.
Hovering rows never exposes full clipboard content through an automatic tooltip.
Expected focus loss hides the popup while modal, menu, and direct-paste transitions do not trigger premature hiding.
Rename, confirmation, error, Settings, and Quick Help flows suppress auto-hide and restore focus after close.
Maximized state and the last restored bounds survive restart without persisting the full-screen rectangle as normal bounds.
Negative coordinates, monitor removal, DPI changes, and maximized drag restore keep the popup recoverable.
An existing schema-v5 database opens without destructive migration and all clips and metadata remain intact.
tags and clip_tags remain present, foreign keys cascade correctly, and the unfinished Tags UI does not alter their data.
Gradle dev launch and the newly built MSI both start successfully with CSS, SVG, runtime, version, and single-instance behavior intact.
Close returns to background, Exit terminates tray/hotkey/executors cleanly, and the next launch starts normally.
